recording.starts: partway through onboarding: the first frame is the goal question already greeting 'Hello Cameron!', so any splash and name entry happened before the recording
recording.after_paywall: Apple sheet dismissed, then a spin-the-wheel exit offer (scripted 10% then 75%), a 75% off countdown offer whose Apple sheet was also dismissed, then the free-tier app with the countdown card on the journal and further in-app paywalls (50% and 76% off).

strategy: Foodvisor runs a long, gentle, chaptered questionnaire (Goal & profile, Your environment, Your habits & behaviour, Your needs) that keeps telling the person their answers are changing their program: live BMI and goal-weight verdicts, a personal summary, and small 'Your program has been updated!' sheets. The arc moves from self-definition and a reassuring body verdict, through lifestyle limits framed as inputs rather than failings, to emotional and identity goals ('build greater self-confidence') right before the price. A science-flavoured loader and a 'We have found your custom program!' beat build anticipation, but the plan itself is only shown as a sales page headed with the person's goal weight. The one idea that carries it is that a personalised program, unlike a generic diet, is what finally works, and every answer visibly feeds that program.

phases.name: Hook and goal
phases.goal: Get the person to define themselves by a goal and their reasons for it within seconds, then reassure them they picked the right app.

phases.name: Body profile and mirror
phases.goal: Collect body data while rewarding each entry with a verdict, hand it back as a flattering summary, then teach that a generic diet fails and a personalised one succeeds.

phases.name: Lifestyle, health, privacy and account
phases.goal: Gather constraints and health conditions while promising low effort and data safety, then secure an account while investment is high.

phases.name: Your environment
phases.goal: Make the person feel their real-life circumstances (location, kids, time, desk job, budget) are understood and factored in, and slip in a referral ask.

phases.name: Your habits and behaviour
phases.goal: Surface eating and exercise habits without shame, show the camera logging as effortless, and lock in small exercise commitments the plan 'adds'.

phases.name: Build and reveal
phases.goal: Make the plan feel earned and evidence-based through a thank-you, a progress bar and science claims, then announce it without showing it.

phases.name: Your needs and identity
phases.goal: Have the person choose the features they want and articulate emotional and identity outcomes in the first person, so the paywall can sell back their own words.

phases.name: Paywall
phases.goal: Present the 'program' as a personal deliverable aimed at their goal weight, remove refund worry, then convert on an annual plan framed per month.

phases.name: Exit offers
phases.goal: Recover a refusal through a gamified 'lucky' discount and a ticking countdown.

phases.name: Free tier with paywalls
phases.goal: Give a first taste of value (calorie goal, logging) while keeping the discount and gated coaching in view.

screens.visual: 5:55 to 6:31: the Coach tab is gated by a peach '50% discount' sheet; 'Unlock my offer' reopens the program sales page now with a green '76% off just for you!' badge (6:00), which leads to the same plan picker at the undiscounted $6.99 / mo and $83.99 (6:04 to 6:10). The person backs out, the journal reloads (6:20) with the countdown still running, then visits Profile (weight chart, goal 170.4 lbs, 2551 Cal / d) and the recording ends in Control Center.
screens.intent: Keeps reselling the same plan from inside the app with three different discount figures (50%, 75%, 76%) in two minutes, one of which leads to full prices; the inconsistency undercuts the urgency it tries to create.

intermission_pattern: Foodvisor uses about ten full-screen intermissions across roughly 37 questions (about one every four questions), plus three answer-triggered bottom sheets ('Your program has been updated!' after the time question, 'Your nutritional goal has been updated!' after active or seated, 'Added to your plan!' after readiness to work out) and two live verdict cards on the weight pickers. They cluster at section boundaries: each coloured chapter opens with a full-bleed section intro in its own colour ('You are in the right place!', 'Your environment has a huge impact...', 'Almost done! Let's talk about...'), and in-section beats are short one-idea statements in serif type with a mascot or diagram. Tone is warm, coach-like and non-judgemental ('we will never tell you to do something that you are not ready for'), and many questions carry a one-line fact or mirror of the person's own data as a preamble, blurring question and intermission. Collectively they build three beliefs before the price: every answer changes the program, a personalised program beats generic diets, and millions of people and science back it. The proof points (32% faster, 73% within 14 days, 4 million users, press logos) are unsourced.
standouts: Screens 9 and 11 put a live verdict card under the weight wheels ('Your BMI: 22.4 Healthy', 'Weight gain: 3% Realistic') that recalculates as the person scrolls, turning data entry into instant feedback.
Screen 10's 'Your personal summary' replays sex, age, height, weight, BMI scale, goal and motivations as chips and a scale bar; the person used it to notice and go back to fix a wrong age.
The answer-triggered bottom sheets after screens 15, 24 and 37 make even 'low' answers (0-5 min a day, mostly seated) feel like they improved the plan rather than exposed a weakness.

Screen 53's spin-the-wheel is scripted to land on 10% first, offer 'Spin Again', then hit the 75% gift, a manufactured-luck exit offer followed by a 9-minute countdown that keeps ticking inside the app.
gaps: The recording starts at the goal question, so any splash, intro carousel or name entry is not shown. The second review card on the paywall is cut off at the right edge ('After 60 days I los[unreadable]'). The Google sign-in round trip at 1:58 to 2:11 returns to 'Create your account' and it is not clear whether sign-in succeeded. Screen 44 briefly shows a 'Set my first goal' button during the transition that may belong to screen 45. The sheets after the paywall exit (5:06 onward) were reviewed by sampling sheets 40 to 56 rather than frame by frame, so they are summarised in three app entries. No new mechanism names were added.
